chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad and ʿAbd Allah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ʿIsa, from ʿAli ibn al-Hakam, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abi Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

It is only upon one of you, when half the night has passed, to rise and perform his salat all together in one sequence: thirteen rakʿahs. Then, if he wishes, he may sit and make du'a; if he wishes, he may sleep; and if he wishes, he may go wherever he wishes.
So this narration came as a concession, lifting the prohibition. What is more excellent, however, is to leave sleeping aside, in accordance with what the other narration contains.

key_terms.اِنْتَصَفَ اللَّيْلُ: when half the night has passed
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat, referring here to the night prayer

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sleep between the rakʿahs of the night prayer and before the morning salat?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling regarding sleeping between the units of the night prayer and before the morning salat. It indicates a concession allowing one to perform the thirteen rakʿahs together and then sleep or engage in du'a, while stating that the more excellent practice is to avoid sleeping, in line with the other narration.
